title: Ode to Joy
source: Beethoven's theme (public domain) with block chords, bass and drums.
stresses: The ordinary case: tune on top, chords in the middle, bass below.

title: Twinkle (Alberti bass)
source: Traditional tune (public domain) over an Alberti bass.
stresses: Two channels only; the accompaniment is a broken chord, not a bass line.

title: Prelude in C, opening (simplified)
source: Opening bars of Bach's Prelude in C, BWV 846 (public domain), simplified to plain sixteenths.
stresses: One channel, no melody at all: pure arpeggio. Is the harmony recovered?

title: Frere Jacques (three-part round)
source: Traditional round (public domain) in three parts, the second part an octave above the first.
stresses: Voices imitate and cross; the first voice is not the highest.

title: Crossing (pad above the tune)
stresses: A sustained pad sits above the tune. Pitch-only methods take the pad for the melody.

title: Dense chords (six-note voicings)
stresses: Six-note chords: far more harmony than three voices can carry.

title: Little Waltz (3/4)
stresses: 3/4 time, bass on the first beat only.

title: Triplets (off the grid)
stresses: Eighth-note triplets do not fit a sixteenth-note grid.

title: Groove (syncopation and drums)
stresses: Syncopated sixteenths, a busy bass and a drum kit.
